_comment: Hub-and-spoke content. The hub signposts; each spoke sells one service to one audience. Wording is the revised editorial pass over Aneesa's approved Stage 2 material, except where marked OWNER — those are structural labels, or slots she has not filled. Nothing is invented: a slot with no source renders its bracketed placeholder so the gap is visible rather than papered over.

brand.triad: the taught word. the spoken word. the written word.

hub.headline: English tuition, narration and writing, delivered with care.
hub.sub: Thoughtful, professional support for students, authors and businesses.
hub.pillarsHeading: Three ways to work with me
hub.pillarsLine: Each service begins with careful attention—to the student, the text or the voice behind the idea.
authorityParagraphs: I am an English teacher, voice artist and writer with 12 years of classroom experience across three countries. My work is grounded in listening closely, identifying what is needed and responding with care.
Before teaching, I acted, performed spoken word and read novels aloud in a care home. Each experience taught me something about language, interpretation and connecting with an audience.

credentials.body: Former teacher in Egypt and Saudi Arabia

services.oneLiner: I identify the gaps holding a student back and build from there, helping them develop the skills and confidence to show what they know.
services.imageAlt: Aneesa writing thoughtfully in a notebook
problem: In a busy classroom, lessons have to keep moving. When a student misses an important step, later work becomes harder and confidence can begin to fall.

The difficulty is often specific: comprehension, exam technique, working within a time limit or knowing how to begin a piece of writing. One-to-one tuition gives us the time to identify it and work on it directly.

aside.heading: Why individual support can help
aside.body: Online resources and classroom support can be useful, but they cannot always respond to the precise gap in front of a student. Individual tuition makes it possible to slow down, try a different explanation and build from a secure foundation.

method.title: A free 20-minute call.
method.body: We discuss what support is needed, the timescale and any current concerns.

method.title: A first session to identify the gaps.
method.body: I assess where the student is now, rather than relying only on where the syllabus says they should be.

method.title: Weekly lessons, booked in blocks.
method.body: Work can be set between sessions and reviewed before the next lesson.

note.heading: Support at every level
note.body: Tuition is not only for students who are struggling. It can also challenge students who are working ahead of their class and need more stimulating material.

services.pricingLine: Lessons are booked in monthly blocks so that each session can build on the last and progress can be reviewed consistently. Rates are confirmed after the introductory call.

agreements.heading: An honest assessment from the beginning.
agreements.body: I will not promise a particular grade before meeting a student. After the first session, I will explain what I have identified, what we can work towards and what that is likely to require.

agreements.heading: Lessons shaped around the student.
agreements.body: We work at the right pace for the individual, with time to revisit or extend material as needed.

agreements.heading: A flexible approach to explanation.
agreements.body: If one explanation does not make sense, I will find another. It is my responsibility to make the learning clear and accessible.

problem: A book can take years to write. Its characters, tone and rhythm deserve a narrator who will understand the work before stepping up to the microphone.
The right performance should feel true to the text, consistent from beginning to end and engaging for the listener.

aside.heading: Why preparation matters
aside.body: An unsuitable tone, inconsistent character voices and avoidable re-recording can all weaken the finished production. Preparation helps the recording process run smoothly and protects the quality of the work.

services.voiceBody: My natural delivery is warm, rich and unhurried, with a clear English accent shaped in Leicester and a pace suited to sustained listening.

method.title: Preparation before recording.

method.title: Recording and delivery.
method.body: Your finished audio is supplied to the agreed technical specification and deadline.

background.heading: Training and experience
background.body: I have trained with voice coach Gary Terzza and studied stage acting at the Television Workshop and Derby Academy. My performance experience also includes spoken word with Beatfreeks and university theatre in England and Canada.

services.oneLiner: I turn voice notes, recordings and existing content into clear, useful writing that still sounds like you.
services.imageAlt: Aneesa reviewing and annotating a manuscript
problem: You have the expertise and the ideas, but turning them into consistent, well-structured content takes time away from the work only you can do.
The challenge is often time and process, not a lack of things to say.

aside.heading: What can get in the way
aside.body: A strong idea is shared once and then lost, or polished so heavily that it no longer sounds like the person behind it.

about.heading: Aneesa
paragraphs: I am an English teacher, voice artist and writer with 12 years of classroom experience across three countries. My work is grounded in listening closely, identifying what is needed and responding with care.
Before teaching, I acted, performed spoken word and read novels aloud in a care home. Each experience taught me something about language, interpretation and connecting with an audience.
about.empathy: As a child, I found time pressure difficult even when I understood the subject. Years later, I needed a teacher to help me learn Arabic despite having access to countless free resources. Both experiences showed me that the right individual support can make all the difference.
about.authority: I have spent 12 years teaching English: in primary classrooms in England, with the British Council in Egypt, at a women's college in Saudi Arabia and at a British secondary school in Doha. I have taught learners from age six to adult, from beginner level through to A-Level.
about.portraitAlt: Aneesa resting her chin on her hands beside an anthology of poetry
why: Classrooms, production schedules and content platforms are designed to serve many people efficiently. That can leave limited space for the needs of one student, the intention behind one book or the individual voice behind an idea.
Working individually creates that space: time to listen, ask thoughtful questions and shape the work around the person or project in front of me.
about.reflectionBody: Outside my client work, I share reading notes, close analysis and reflections on the books and passages that stay with me.
